title.narrative: Integrated Health, Nutrition, WASH and MPCA support to IDPs in Mekelle City IDPs, Abiy Adi town IDPs, and Northwest Zone, Asgede woreda IDPs, Tigray Region, Ethiopia.

description.narrative: ltpgtFollowing two years of conflict (Nov 2020–Nov 2022), over 760,000 individuals remain internally displaced across the Tigray region, hosted in overcrowded, makeshift shelters. According to the Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) Round 38, the Northwestern, Central, and Mekelle zones host the largest numbers of IDPs. A multisectoral assessment in late 2024 highlighted severe gaps in food, shelter, health, and WASH services. Displaced populations are living in schools, abandoned buildings, and other inadequate shelters, often facing evictions and protection risks.ltbrgtAt the Quiha IDP site in Mekelle, 527 IDPs including children, the elderly, and persons with disabilities, faced eviction in early 2025 after the land was reassigned. As of March, 75 shelters were dismantled, forcing multiple households to share single rooms. A rapid shelter assessment at Seba Kare (70 Kare) IDP site identified 163 vacant shelters and others requiring minor to major repairs. A relocation preference survey showed 85 Quiha households favoring relocation to 70 Kare, while 66 households opted for host community integration with rental support.ltbrgtTo address urgent needs, the clusters prioritized assistance in Mekelle (SC4), Abiy Adi town (TVET, Metal Shade, Animal Shade, Preparatory, Edaga Robue, Sur, and Kola Tembien), and Asgede Woreda (Adi Mehameday and Hitsats). Cluster-endorsed interventions include:ltbrgtltbgtWASH:lt/bgt Acute shortages of water and sanitation. Many sites practice open defecation. IRC is rehabilitating pipelines, installing water tanks, and distributing treatment chemicals. Latrines at SC4 are overflowing and require desludging.ltbrgtltbgtShelter/ES-NFI:lt/bgt Widespread shelter degradation, especially in Abiy Adi and Asgede. IRC is distributing 604 pre-positioned kits and procuring 250 additional kits, including for persons with disabilities. Materials from Quiha are repurposed for SC4 IDPs.ltbrgtltbgtHealth:lt/bgt Essential drug shortages and minimal service access. The Tigray Health Bureau has prioritized Quiha, SC4, and Abiy Adi health facilities for supply distribution and proposed MHNTs to operate from these centers to serve IDPs effectively.ltbrgtltbgtCash Assistance:lt/bgt 66 Quiha households will receive rental support. The Cash Working Group has prioritized Abiy Adi and Asgede for additional interventions.ltbrgtIn Abiy Adi town, over 10,800 IDP households face dire conditions with limited food, WASH, and shelter access. In Asgede Woreda, the Adi Mehameday and Hitsats IDP sites host over 40,000 individuals. Only partial food aid has reached them, and nutrition levels are above emergency thresholds (GAM 29.9%, SAM 2.78%, MAM 27.18%). Shelter assessments show extreme degradation, with frequent flooding and risk of collapse due to prolonged lack of repair.ltbrgtWater access remains limited. IDPs at several sites rely on unsafe river water, and some pipelines are non-functional. At connected sites like Preparatory and Edaga Robue, water supply is irregular and impacted by unpaid bills. IRC has been endorsed to cover utility costs to sustain access.ltbrgtOverall, this project aims to deliver coordinated WASH, Shelter/ESNFI, Health, and Cash interventions to address the urgent needs of displaced communities in Tigray. Interventions are guided by recent assessments, cluster priorities, and consultations with IDP communities and local authorities, ensuring an inclusive, needs-based response that enhances protection and dignity for affected populations. ltbrgtlt/pgt
